subject: SCIENCE
title: Five Sense Helpers
objective: Connect primary sense organs with observations while recognizing senses work together.
introduction: Milo hears a bird sing and smells a mango! Which sense organ helped him do each one?

vocabulary.definition: How we learn — seeing, hearing, touching, tasting, smelling.
What you hear with your ears.
The sense that lets us listen with our ears.

items.prompt: Which statement about the senses is true?

options.text: Taste works without smell in every way
Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin are primary helpers, and senses often work together.

items.explanation: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin each help you sense, and they often work together — taste works closely with smell, and people sense in their own way.

items.prompt: Which pair matches a sense organ to its job?
items.explanation: Eyes see light and color. Ears hear sound, and the tongue tastes.

options.text: Taste works without smell in every way

items.explanation: Smell and taste work together — taste is weaker when you cannot smell. Eyes do see light and color, and ears do hear sound.

items.prompt: Which organ primarily helps detect sound?
items.explanation: Ears are the organs that pick up sound. Eyes see, and the tongue tastes.

items.prompt: Which pair matches a sense organ to what it senses?
items.explanation: Skin senses touch — it does not hear sound, and eyes see light and color.
